content.title: US annual PPI inflation rises to 4% in March vs. 4.6% expected
content.text: TRENDING:Oil priceXAU/USDEUR/USDTrade WarSilverGBP/USDAUD/USDNewsletterUpgradeLoginProducer inflation in the United States, as measured by the change in the Producer Price Index (PPI), rose to 4% on a yearly basis in March from 3.4% in February, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Tuesday. This reading came in below the market expectation of 4.6%. On a monthly basis, the PPI rose 0.5%, matching February's increase and falling short of analysts' estimate of 1.2%.Other details of the report showed that the PPI ex Food & Energy was up 3.8% YoY in March, compared to the market forecast of 4.2%.Market reactionThe US Dollar Index (DXY) remains under bearish pressure following this data and was last seen losing 0.35% on the day at 98.03.AuthorEren SengezerFXStreetAs an economist at heart, Eren Sengezer specializes in the assessment of the short-term and long-term impacts of macroeconomic data, central bank policies and political developments on financial assets.More from Eren SengezerShare:Legal TextRelated contentAUD/USD climbs on extended US-Iran ceasefire, firm RBA rate hike expectationsGhiles GuezoutUSD/JPY steadies as Middle East tensions offset softer yieldsAgustin WazneGold trades range-bound after bounce from weekly low as US-Iran uncertainty persistsVishal ChaturvediGBP/USD steadies as Iran deadlock keeps Dollar bid in checkChristian Borjon ValenciaECB: Growth risks temper hike urgency – Societe GeneraleFXStreet Insights TeamEUR/GBP weakens as UK CPI lifts GBP; technicals signal downside below 200-day SMAVishal ChaturvediEditor's PicksEUR/USD extends slide toward 1.1700 as optimism fades EUR/USD comes under renewed bearish pressure and drops toward 1.1700 in the American session on Wednesday.
